texts.preamble: Vinod Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan And Anr on 7 March, 2017 Author: Pankaj Bhandari Bench: Pankaj Bhandari High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan Bench At Jaipur S.B.Criminal Miscellaneous (Petition) No. 1405 / 2014 Vinod Kumar S/o Shri Vasudev, B/c Mahajan, Resident of Chawani Bazar, Jhunjhunu. Accused-Petitioner Versus 1.State Of Rajasthan through Public Prosecutor Non-Petitioner 2.Food Inspector through Chief Medical & Health Officer, Jhunjhunu. C o m p l a i n a n t - N o n - P e t i t i o n e r _____________________________________________________ For Petitioner(s) : Mr. B h a r a t S a i n i F o r R e s p o n d e n t ( s ) : M r . R i s h i R a j S i n g h , P . P . _____________________________________________________ Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pankaj Bhandari Judgment 07/03/2017
texts.facts: 1. Petitioner has filed this miscellaneous petition aggrieved by order dated 25.09.2013, passed by Sessions Judge, Jhunjhunu, in Criminal Revision No. 84/2013, whereby the revision petition preferred by the petitioner was dismissed and order dated 12.08.2013, whereby the charge has been framed against the accused-petitioner under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was upheld. 2.
texts.arguments: It is contended by counsel for the petitioner that petitioner is a dealer, his case is similar to that of the retailer who has been discharged as per the Act. It is contended that as per Sub-Section 2 of Section 19 vendor shall not be deem to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated food, if he proves (2 of 3) [CRLMP-1405/2014] that article of food while in his possession was stored and that it was sold in the same state as he purchased it. 3. It is further contended that this benefit has been given to the retailer, but has not been given to the petitioner as the petitioner at that relevant time was unable to produce the bills vide which he has purchased the "Ghee". It is contended that the petitioner be given an opportunity to produce the original bills before the concerned Court and the concerned Court be directed now to reconsider the prayer of the petitioner with regard to the framing of charge. 4. Sub-Clause 2 of Section 19 provides that if a vendor proves that he has purchased the article of food from a distributor or dealer with warranty in the prescribed form and the article of food while in his possession was properly stored and he sold it in the same state as he purchased it, then he deem to any offence.
